James Henderson has created the first draft at this template and it will now be tweaked: 
Market research 
Engage with Sales – specifically around what they’re seeing in publications, what the competition are doing, in their opinion what has landed and what will land, and how best they would use this to present the value of Puzzel 
Engage with Account Management – what are our customers in this vertical actually using? What do they like? What do they want? On service reviews, what have they presented about their strategy going forward? 
Engage with Marketing – How can the above scenarios fit in to broader messaging around Puzzel? 
 
Scenario planning 
This is a collaborative process with the AEs representing this vertical.  
Firstly, design 5 scenarios. Not every scenario needs to include every module we can think of.  
A good narrative across the scenarios is ‘these are the problems we’re solving for LIVE customers’ > ‘this is what the vertical is moving towards right now’ > ‘this is the future of the vertical’. This allows us to position ourselves as vertical leaders and show the value of Puzzel USPs such as DE. 
Work together to create a brief. Typically this is a document detailing each demo scenario blow-by-blow – more of a user guide. 
Work together to create ‘Problem > what we show > the value it brings’ slides. These are key when presenting to new business – you won’t be walking through Puzzel feature by feature, so tell-show-tell will prevent the prospect from getting lost. 
Aim for 5 scenarios, that can be ran through in anywhere from 5-15 minutes each, depending on the context of the meeting. 
 
Demo building 
Put these scenarios together! Ideally this will live on a separate tenant. This means anybody can log in and demo to the same effect, and it also stops demo clashes. 
Create other assets needed, such as website pages, or tailored DE banners – start this early as it may need others, i.e Michal, or the DE team. 
After iteration 1 of each scenario is complete, record them, complete with talk track, and share with sales team and colleagues for feedback. 
In parallel to this, the AEs should be updating their slideware. 
 
Iterating – internal 
Ensure a running cadence with the relevant AEs. Run through each demo scenario, and tailor as feedback dictates. 
Update your demo assets, and document as necessary. 
Once built, rehearse both demo scenarios and slideware, to ensure any proper demos are seamless. 
At this time it would be appropriate to make a technical document too, to ensure other SEs can pick up and go. 
 
Iterating – partners 
Run the same process as above, but with partners this time. They’ll have a less Puzzel-centric view than your colleagues. Additionally, this will drum up interest in Puzzel’s new approach. 
Update demo assets and documentation. 
 
Iterating – prospects 
Here’s the exciting part! Run these past a prospect. 
Catch up after with the AE. What landed? What could have been smoother? What caused confusion, and what warranted a deep dive? 
Iterate and go again! 
 
Future 
Work on creating more scenarios. There are more than 5 use cases per vertical, and as our understanding of the vertical/demo success grows, as should our demo suite.
